stem: A zero-coupon bond will pay Rs 12,155 at maturity in 2 years. The market discount rate is 10% per annum compounded semi-annually. What is the fair present value of this bond today?  [Given: (1.05)^4 = 1.2155]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Discounting at 10% annually for 2 periods (n=2) gives 12155/(1.1)^2 = 12155/1.21 = Rs 10,046 ~ Rs 11,050 if the student uses just one year; using n=1 at 10% annual gives 12155/1.1 = Rs 11,050, mixing up periods.
Semi-annual rate i = 10%/2 = 5%, n = 2 x 2 = 4 half-year periods. PV = 12155 / (1.05)^4 = 12155 / 1.2155 = Rs 10,000.

Discounting for only 3 semi-annual periods instead of 4 gives 12155/(1.05)^3 = 12155/1.1576 = Rs 10,498; rounding and slight variation produces Rs 10,988 if n=2 annual periods at 5% is used instead: 12155/(1.05)^2 = 12155/1.1025 = Rs 11,024.
Using the face value Rs 12,155 directly as today's value ignores all discounting.

explanation: When the rate is nominal annual but compounding is semi-annual, convert: i = 10%/2 = 5% per half-year, n = 2 years x 2 = 4 half-year periods. PV = 12155 / (1.05)^4 = 12155 / 1.2155 = Rs 10,000.

explanation_sections.punchline: Semi-annual compounding means dividing the annual rate by 2 AND doubling the number of periods before discounting.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: PV = FV / (1+i)^n. Decisive move - rate-period conversion: nominal 10% p.a. semi-annual => i = 5% per period, n = 4 periods. Apply given: (1.05)^4 = 1.2155. PV = 12,155/1.2155 = Rs 10,000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always match rate and period: semi-annual compounding requires halving the annual rate and doubling n.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 seconds. One conversion step then direct division. Trap: option 1 uses annual rate with only 1 period.
